text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000132's 99215 rate is elevated within every complexity tier, including patients with no chronic conditions, but records came back for too few claims to show whether the notes support the billed levels.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans away from a sicker-panel explanation: the excess 99215 share holds at every condition count, not just among multi-morbid patients, and the low-complexity sample includes 99215s for routine-looking problems such as upper respiratory infection, rash, UTI and follow-up visits (e.g., C0063973, C0064384, C0065183, C0064571). The documentation cannot yet confirm or refute this, since only a handful of 99215 charts were reviewed. One chart (C0064985) was documented below the billed level. One chart documented as high MDM (C0062714) is a 22-year-old with no chronic conditions billed for low back pain, which is worth checking for inflated or templated notes, as are the few moderate-plus data-reviewed notes with no lab or test line. A reviewer should first request a larger targeted chart sample of 99215 claims on patients with 0 to 1 conditions, checking whether MDM and time are genuinely recorded. They should also look at the heavy 99214 volume, which the 99215 screen does not address."}
